owners.bounds: Memory admission is min(10000, configured spool capacity). Durable capacity is the configured per-node entry cap; destination copies are separate records and retries retain ownership until acknowledgment.
64 shared write slots. Admission and sink completion share capacity; a caller timeout does not release an unfinished sink write.

Pending events have no fixed bound. The 30-second writer and shutdown flush retain detached ownership through physical newline writes, cleanup and logging; partial or interrupted writes retain lower-bound losses.

Distinct dirty or deleted IPs have no fixed bound. Coalesced current intent and detached writes stay owned through I/O and retry reconciliation; failed writes retained in memory are not durable across process exit.
One shared block-state owner, with no fixed cap on waiting callers. Progress follows individual firewall, state and cleanup operations without taking their locks during health reads.

Distinct IPs retained for deferred bookkeeping after a flush have no fixed cap. Actual cleanup remains in flight until state outcomes settle; unknown reads expose unavailable depth and lower-bound loss.

1000 durable pending retries; admitted candidates have no fixed aggregate cap. Current-policy refusals complete without loss; record outcomes are settled against durable state, retaining uncertainty after unreadable writes.

5000 waiting records with drop-oldest overflow. Configured interval is intentional waiting. Detached preparation and each configured notification remain owned independently, including live delivery and late admissions after the ticker stops.
256 waiting verifications and one active worker. DNS and cache writes retain ownership; duplicates share the original age and expected negative answers are not losses.
256 decoded events per active backend. A received event stays in flight through evaluation and finding admission. Kernel rings are separate stages.

Each active ring reports its loaded map capacity and occupancy in bytes, separately from decoded output. Reservation losses and unconsumed shutdown submissions are retained; final loss can be a lower bound.
256 waiting annotations and four callbacks. Duplicates share pending identity and age; failed annotation does not discard its finding.
1024 waiting actions and one active handler. Feed refresh cannot hide admitted actions; shutdown accounts for queued and active work.
Each host or account batch has its configured runner limit. Concurrent batches have no fixed global capacity; waiting checks and occupied wrappers retain separate execution deadlines.
Aggregate capacity is unavailable: timed-out check functions can outlive runner slots. Function and caller must both settle before ownership ends.
One live baseline scan slot. Waiting callers have no fixed cap; actual filesystem work, result handling and persistence retain ownership through cancellation.
Five site inventory workers per refresh and a finite discovered-site batch. Concurrent refreshes have no fixed aggregate cap. Shared-refresh waiters belong to check executions.
At most five admitted queries per scan. Concurrent scans have no fixed aggregate cap; quota-admitted work stays owned through response cleanup and result persistence.

Five checksum workers per discovered-installation batch. Concurrent scans have no fixed combined capacity. Each installation remains owned through the bounded command, integrity result collection and verified-file caching; actual timeout and interrupted-command failures count once.
Per-message engine batches have finite result buffers, but concurrent messages and engines outliving timeouts have no fixed aggregate cap. Both result handoffs retain work.
Three shared hash-verification slots, retained until KDF and caller finish. Waiting callers have no fixed global cap and use the audit deadline.
Five active mailbox audits per scan; concurrent scans have no fixed aggregate capacity. Ownership includes result collection and cache writes.
Aggregate of live subscriber capacities; daemon streams use 64 findings each. Running writes remain owned through encoding and flush.
Analyzer channel capacity is selected at monitor construction. Waiting producers and active analyzers retain event ownership through finding delivery and failure.
16384 candidate slots and 16384 held findings. Lag starts after eligibility; detached probes and emission batches remain running. Retry, refusal and shutdown outcomes preserve loss history.
1024 waiting directory tasks. Coalescence preserves age; detached scans stay running while new work queues independently, including the same directory.
20000 staged-file slots are shared by waiting and detached verification batches. Retries preserve queue age and reserved capacity; shutdown waits for analyzer admissions.
Finding channel capacity is selected at daemon construction. Blocked producers, held batches and active dispatch remain owned outside the channel; intentional scan-warning filtering is not loss.
One ordered incident writer. Immutable waiting snapshots and coalesced deferred bookkeeping have no fixed global cap; completion signals only order snapshots owned outside their channels.
64 records per selected reader. In-flight ownership includes parsing and finding delivery; replacements retain known record loss. Unread source history belongs to the separate source rows.
Untransferred file bytes have no fixed queue capacity. Descriptor sampling includes disk, read-ahead and raw partial bytes; generation changes retain uncertain loss history.
Journal cursors expose neither exact unread count nor capacity. Cursor, selected entry, wait, delivery and cleanup own progress while historical uncertainty remains explicit.
Kernel pending-record count has unknown group capacity. The reader owns detached batches through dispatch; shutdown record losses are lower bounds.
Inotify reports pending bytes, with unknown capacity and lower-bound losses. Read batches remain owned through callbacks and descriptor cleanup.
Inotify reports pending bytes, with unknown capacity and lower-bound losses. Read batches remain owned through callbacks and descriptor cleanup.
Kernel pending-record count has unknown group capacity. The reader owns detached batches through dispatch; shutdown record losses are lower bounds.
One worker RPC at a time; lock waiters have no fixed global cap. Requests retain pipe operations after caller timeout and remain owned through decoding and child cleanup.
100000 durable findings per state directory. Pending writes and deliveries awaiting acknowledgment retain ownership; retries preserve enqueue age.
4096 waiting attribution writes. Each transaction has at most 256 operations, including explicit flush. Flush barriers order existing writes; concurrent arrivals cannot extend a flush indefinitely.
1024 waiting requests and two process workers. Oldest queued requests may be replaced; active work includes reads, observation, account resolution and cache writes.
64 shared deadline-limited process-read slots. Underlying I/O and caller must both finish before release; synchronous reads consume no slot.
Eight waiting full-scan jobs and one worker. Admission callers have no fixed global cap. Ownership includes job persistence, check batches, remediation and cleanup.
64 shared deadline-limited resolver slots, retained until resolver and caller finish. Cache hits and synchronous lookup mode add no queued work.
Scanner channel capacity is selected at spool watcher construction. Running scans and known losses survive watcher replacement.

The durable shutdown file retains the newest 10000 findings. Concurrent appends and detached replay have no fixed aggregate bound. Parked age is intentional; operations remain owned through readback, clear, replay and interruption settlement.
